questions: What are the closest existing methods to our proposed local context subgraph enrichment and adaptive repair loop?
Is the idea novel, or has it been explored under other terminology (e.g., context-aware triple training, subgraph-based QA training)?
What baselines and evaluation methodology (datasets, metrics) are appropriate for evaluating our approach?
Is the proposed method feasible to implement and test given current computational resources and available datasets?
What potential confounding factors could affect the interpretation of results (e.g., effects of longer training, different data distributions)?
search_topics: knowledge graph question answering with local context
adaptive repair loop in knowledge graph QA
reinforcement learning for multi-hop QA transfer
subgraph size impact on QA performance
contextual triple training for multi-hop reasoning
comparison_targets: Baseline: training on isolated triples (standard KGQA embedding methods)
Subgraph retrieval methods (e.g., SR from arxiv:2202.13296)
Context-aware QA methods (e.g., Retrieve, Summarize, Plan; GRASP)
RL-based QA methods (e.g., Tackling Distractor Documents with RL)
Existing multi-hop QA models (e.g., NSM, TransE)
